concepts.def: The variety of life in an area.
Energy passes through food chains, lost at each level.
Carbon and nitrogen recycled through ecosystems.
Groups of a species; size limited by resources.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Living Environment — a core area of A-Level Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Living Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Living Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The variety of living organisms in an area, from genes to ecosystems, is called:
options: Biodiversity
Carrying capacity
Residence time
Albedo

mcqs.q: Green plants that make their own food sit at which trophic level?
options: Producers
Primary consumers
Secondary consumers
Decomposers

mcqs.q: A species whose loss would dramatically alter its whole ecosystem is a:
options: Keystone species
Pioneer species
Invasive species
Indicator species

mcqs.q: A network of interconnected food chains is best described as a:
options: Food web
A single food chain
Nutrient cycle
Trophic pyramid

mcqs.q: Why is only about 10% of energy passed to the next trophic level?
options: Invasive species are always beneficial to ecosystems.
Energy is created at each trophic level.
Most energy is lost as heat through respiration and in undigested material, so little is available to the next level.
All the energy is passed on with nothing lost.

mcqs.q: Are invasive species always more harmful than native species?
options: Not inherently, but they can be very damaging where they lack natural predators and outcompete native species.
Biodiversity only counts the number of plants.
Native species are always the harmful ones.
Invasive species are always beneficial to ecosystems.

mcqs.q: Does high biodiversity make an ecosystem more stable?
options: No; biodiversity has no link to ecosystem stability.
Generally yes; greater diversity often gives more resilience to disturbance, though it is not guaranteed.
Energy is created at each trophic level.
Biodiversity only counts the number of plants.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Conservation”?
options: A species whose presence has a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem, so that its loss would dramatically change the community.
The protection and careful management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity, for example through nature reserves and breeding programmes.
A community of living organisms together with the non-living physical environment, interacting as a system through energy flow and nutrient cycling.
A feeding position in a food chain, such as producer, primary consumer or secondary consumer, through which energy passes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Trophic level”?
options: A species whose presence has a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem, so that its loss would dramatically change the community.
A feeding position in a food chain, such as producer, primary consumer or secondary consumer, through which energy passes.
The protection and careful management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity, for example through nature reserves and breeding programmes.
The variety of living organisms in an area, measured at the level of genes, species and ecosystems, and an indicator of ecological health.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Keystone species”?
options: The variety of living organisms in an area, measured at the level of genes, species and ecosystems, and an indicator of ecological health.
A species whose presence has a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem, so that its loss would dramatically change the community.
A community of living organisms together with the non-living physical environment, interacting as a system through energy flow and nutrient cycling.
The protection and careful management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity, for example through nature reserves and breeding programmes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ecosystem”?
options: A community of living organisms together with the non-living physical environment, interacting as a system through energy flow and nutrient cycling.
A feeding position in a food chain, such as producer, primary consumer or secondary consumer, through which energy passes.
The variety of living organisms in an area, measured at the level of genes, species and ecosystems, and an indicator of ecological health.
The protection and careful management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity, for example through nature reserves and breeding programmes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Food web”?
options: A feeding position in a food chain, such as producer, primary consumer or secondary consumer, through which energy passes.
The protection and careful management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity, for example through nature reserves and breeding programmes.
A network of interconnected food chains showing the feeding relationships and flow of energy between organisms in a community.
A community of living organisms together with the non-living physical environment, interacting as a system through energy flow and nutrient cycling.

options: A feeding position in a food chain, such as producer, primary consumer or secondary consumer, through which energy passes.
The protection and careful management of habitats and species to maintain biodiversity, for example through nature reserves and breeding programmes.
The variety of living organisms in an area, measured at the level of genes, species and ecosystems, and an indicator of ecological health.
A network of interconnected food chains showing the feeding relationships and flow of energy between organisms in a community.
